1.title: No single leader
1.text: Judges opens after Joshua's death: with no leader over all Israel, each tribe had to take possession of its own inheritance.

1.question: Which tribe did the Lord say should go up first against the Canaanites?
options: Judah
Benjamin
Ephraim
Dan

1.question: What did Adoni-bezek acknowledge after his thumbs were cut off?
options: That God repaid him as he had done to other kings
That the Israelites were unjust in treating him so
That he would soon reign again over the Canaanites
That the gods of Canaan had forsaken him

1.question: Who took Kirjath-sepher and received Achsah as wife?
options: Othniel
Caleb
Simeon
Judah

1.question: Why did Judah fail to drive out the inhabitants of the valley?
options: They had chariots of iron
The walls were too high
They lacked soldiers
Egypt defended them

1.question: What did Israel do with the Canaanites when it grew strong, instead of driving them out?
options: Put them to tribute
Took them to Egypt
Made them allies
Made them priests

1.question: Which tribe did the Amorites force into the mountains, not letting them come to the valley?
options: Dan
Judah
Levi
Reuben

2.title: What a 'judge' is
2.text: In this book a 'judge' does not preside over courts: he is a deliverer raised up by God to save Israel from oppressors and to lead it.

2.question: What did the angel of the Lord rebuke at Bochim?
options: Israel's leagues and not throwing down the altars
Israel failing to build the temple at the proper time
Israel leaving Canaan too soon after fully entering it
Israel asking for a king before its due time

2.question: How old was Joshua, the servant of the Lord, when he died?
options: 110 years
90 years
70 years
120 years

2.template: they forsook the Lord, and served Baal and {0}

2.question: What happened repeatedly after a judge died?
options: The people corrupted themselves and followed other gods
The people built a new altar in honor of the fallen judge's name
The people chose another judge among the elders of the tribes
The people remembered the commandments with zeal

2.question: Why did the Lord leave nations undriven-out?
options: To prove whether Israel would keep his way
To enrich Israel with the spoil of the nations
To punish Joshua for his failures in leadership
To divide the land equally among the tribes

3.title: 'The land had rest'
3.text: Each cycle ends with a refrain: after the judge delivers Israel, 'the land had rest' for 40 or 80 years — until the next relapse.

3.question: Which peoples did the Lord leave to prove Israel and teach it war?
options: Philistines, Canaanites, Sidonians and Hivites
Egyptians, Amalekites and Midianites from the desert
Babylonians, Assyrians and Egyptians from the plains
Edomites and Ammonites from the neighboring hills

3.question: Who was the first judge, who defeated Chushan-rishathaim?
options: Othniel
Ehud
Shamgar
Barak

3.question: How many years did Israel serve Eglon king of Moab?
options: 18 years
8 years
40 years
80 years

3.question: How did Ehud kill Eglon king of Moab?
options: With a two-edged dagger hidden on his right thigh
By hanging him with a rope while he slept in the tent
By strangling him quickly with his own royal garments
By pushing him off a very high cliff nearby

3.question: Why did Eglon's servants delay before entering the parlour?
options: They thought he was relieving himself
They heard him praying in a loud voice
They feared Ehud and dared not go near
They awaited orders from the king himself

3.question: Who killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad?
options: Shamgar
Ehud
Othniel
Barak

4.title: The only female judge
4.text: Deborah is the only woman among Israel's judges — a prophetess who judged the people under a palm tree and led the nation to victory.

4.template: {0}, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel

4.question: What did Deborah tell Barak, who would only go to war if she went too?
options: The honor of the victory would go to a woman
He would die in battle before the day was over
The Lord would not go with him or with his army
He would lose the throne and the people's trust

4.question: Whom did the Lord deliver into Barak's hand at mount Tabor?
options: Sisera and his chariots
Heber the Kenite and his tent
The king of Canaan and his court
The captains of Sisera

4.question: Who hid Sisera in her tent and gave him milk?
options: Jael
Deborah
Sisera's mother
Achsah

4.question: How did Jael kill Sisera while he slept?
options: She drove a tent stake through his temple
With a sharp double-edged sword she carried
With a bow and a heavily poisoned iron arrow
With poison mixed into his cup of milk

5.title: 'A mother in Israel'
5.text: In the song Deborah calls herself 'a mother in Israel.' Chapter 5 is poetry — one of the Bible's oldest passages — retelling the victory of chapter 4.

5.question: What is Judges chapter 5?
options: A song of Deborah and Barak celebrating the victory
A list of laws given by Moses to the people of Israel
A complete genealogy of the twelve tribes of Israel
A prayer of Sisera before the final battle

5.question: According to the song, what brought war to Israel's gates?
options: Choosing new gods
Famine across the land
Lack of water in the hills
Joshua's death up north

5.question: Whom does the song call to awake and utter a song?
options: Deborah
Jael
Naomi
Rachel

5.template: the stars in their courses fought against {0}

5.question: Whom did the angel of the Lord command to be cursed for not coming to help?
options: Meroz
Moab
Edom
Amalek

5.question: Who, at the song's end, looked out the window waiting for the chariot that never returned?
options: Sisera's mother
Deborah
Jael
Jabin's daughter

6.title: Hiding at the winepress
6.text: Gideon was threshing wheat hidden in a winepress, fearing Midian, when the angel greeted him as a 'mighty man of valour.'

6.question: Who oppressed Israel, coming like locusts to destroy the harvests?
options: The Midianites
The Philistines
The Moabites
The Amorites

6.question: What did God send to the people before raising up Gideon?
options: A prophet to rebuke them
A foreign army to subdue them
An angel to announce judgment on them
A famine to make them repent

6.question: How did the angel of the Lord greet Gideon?
options: 'The Lord is with thee, mighty man of valour'
'Arise and destroy the altars of Baal'
'Fear not, for great signs I will give thee'
'Go and free thy captive people'

6.question: What confirmed to Gideon that he spoke with the angel of the Lord?
options: Fire rose from the rock and consumed the offering
A cloud descended and covered the whole valley
The earth shook and a river split in two
A voice thundered from the oak tree

6.question: What did Gideon do by night at the Lord's command?
options: He tore down his father's altar of Baal
He rebuilt the altar of Baal with new stones
He consulted the elders of the city about the altar
He hid the wooden idol on the mountain

6.question: What did the men of the city demand on learning Gideon had torn down the altar?
options: That he be put to death
That he be crowned
That he rebuild the altar in gold
That he leave the city

6.question: What came upon Gideon so that he gathered the army?
options: The Spirit of the Lord
A dream
A pillar of fire
An order from Pharaoh

6.question: What sign did Gideon ask with the fleece of wool?
options: The fleece wet and the ground dry, then the reverse
That fire would come down from heaven upon the fleece
That the fleece stay dry and the ground always wet
That the fleece shine like the moon at night

7.title: 300 against a multitude
7.text: From 32,000 men God reduced Gideon's army to just 300 — so the victory would clearly be his, not Israel's strength.

7.question: Why did the Lord have Gideon reduce the army?
options: So Israel could not vaunt that its own hand had saved it
So that the Midianites could not prepare their defenses in time
So that the priests could offer sacrifices of victory beforehand
To spare the families from greater losses in battle

7.question: How were the 300 men chosen?
options: They were those who lapped the water with the hand
They were chosen by the order in which they came forward
They were those who knelt down before the river to drink
They were selected among the twelve tribes

7.question: What dream of a Midianite encouraged Gideon?
options: A cake of barley bread that overturned the tent
An army of angels surrounding the whole camp
A flaming sword that crossed the whole sky
A strong wind that tore up the tents

7.question: With what did the 300 attack the camp of Midian?
options: Trumpets and pitchers with torches inside
Bonfires lit all around the entire valley
Drums and standards bearing royal emblems
Spears and fiery torches lit brightly

7.question: Which princes of Midian were slain in the pursuit?
options: Oreb and Zeeb
Zebah and Zalmunna
Sisera and Jabin
Gog and Magog

8.title: Gideon refuses the throne
8.text: Gideon refused to be king, saying only the Lord should rule over Israel — yet the golden ephod he made ended up leading the people astray.

8.question: Which tribe complained at not being called to the battle against Midian?
options: Ephraim
Judah
Dan
Benjamin

8.question: What did the men of Succoth deny Gideon's weary soldiers?
options: Bread
Water
Weapons
Horses

8.question: Which two kings of Midian did Gideon capture?
options: Zebah and Zalmunna
Oreb and Zeeb
Sisera and Jabin
Gog and Magog

8.question: What did Gideon do to Succoth and Penuel?
options: He punished them for refusing help
He rewarded them for offering bread
He appointed their elders as new judges
He forgave them and continued his journey

8.question: What did Gideon answer when they wanted to make him king?
options: 'I will not rule, nor my son; the Lord shall rule over you'
'I will be king if all the people swear to obey only the law of Moses'
'I will accept the throne if the seventy elders of Israel anoint me'
'My son will reign after me, but I never shall'

8.question: What did Gideon make from the spoil's gold, which became a snare to Israel?
options: An ephod
A golden calf
A sword
A throne

8.question: How long did the land have rest in Gideon's days?
options: Forty years
Eighty years
Twenty years
Seven years

9.title: Killed by a millstone
9.text: Abimelech died when a woman cast a piece of a millstone on his head; wounded, he asked his armourbearer to kill him, so none could say a woman slew him.

9.question: What did Abimelech do to his seventy brothers to become king?
options: He killed them on one stone
He shut them in a tower and burned it
He banished them to a foreign land
He imprisoned them in Shechem

9.question: In Jotham's parable, what were the trees seeking?
options: A king to reign over them
Shade to protect their young ones
A leader to guide them through the storm
Fruit to feed the birds

9.question: In Jotham's parable, which plant agreed to reign over the trees?
options: The bramble
The olive tree
The fig tree
The vine

9.question: What did Jotham wish, in his curse, between Abimelech and the men of Shechem?
options: That fire would come out and consume them mutually
That lasting peace would reign between them forevermore
That Abimelech would govern them with wisdom and justice
That the two would live together in total harmony

9.question: How long did Abimelech rule over Israel?
options: Three years
Forty years
Seven years
Twenty years

9.question: Who rose up in Shechem and defied Abimelech?
options: Gaal the son of Ebed
Zebul the son of Abimelech
Zalmunna the son of Zebul
A son of Jerubbaal

9.question: Who warned Abimelech of Gaal's revolt in Shechem?
options: Zebul
Jotham
Gideon
Joash

9.question: What did Zebul tell Gaal about what he saw coming down the mountains?
options: That it was only the morning fog rising over the fields
That they were shadows of the mountains
That they were travelers coming from Shechem
That it was only the wind blowing

9.question: What happened to Gaal after the battle?
options: He was driven out of Shechem
He died fighting against Abimelech
He was captured and taken to Thebez
He hid inside the tower

9.question: How did those who took refuge in the tower of Shechem die?
options: Abimelech burned the tower over them
They were killed by the sword by soldiers
They died of hunger during the long siege
They surrendered and were all forgiven

9.question: To which tower did Abimelech go to attack next, where he would meet his death?
options: Thebez
Shechem
Ophrah
Succoth

9.question: How does the book sum up Abimelech's death?
options: God requited the wickedness he did to his brothers
It was divine punishment for the idolatry of the people
It was Zebul's own personal revenge against Abimelech
It was the result of an old family curse

10.title: The minor judges
10.text: Tola and Jair are 'minor judges,' told in only a few verses. Jair had thirty sons and thirty cities, called Havoth-jair.

10.question: Which judges are named at the start of chapter 10?
options: Tola and Jair
Othniel and Ehud
Shamgar and Barak
Deborah and Gideon

10.question: Israel's idolatry led to oppression by which peoples in this chapter?
options: Philistines and Ammonites
Egyptians and Edomites
Babylonians and Assyrians
Canaanites and Hivites

10.question: What did the Lord answer, with irony, when Israel cried out again?
options: 'Go and cry unto the gods which ye have chosen'
'I will send you a judge to deliver you immediately'
'I am no longer your God, nor will I hear you now'
'I will forgive you just this one time'

10.question: What did Israel do before the Lord's soul was grieved for their misery?
options: It put away the strange gods and served the Lord
It built an altar in honor of Baal and Ashtoreth
It sent ambassadors to ask the Philistines for help
It fasted and prayed for forty long days

11.title: A rash vow
11.text: Jephthah promised to offer whatever first came out of his house when he returned in victory — and it was his only daughter who came out to meet him with timbrels.

11.question: Why did Jephthah's brothers drive him from home?
options: Because he was the son of another woman
Because he had sold their father's inheritance
Because he had rebelled against their father's authority
Because he refused to fight alongside them

11.question: What did the elders of Gilead ask of Jephthah?
options: To be their head in war against the Ammonites
To gather an army to attack the fierce Midianites
To negotiate peace with the king of the Ammonites
To rebuild the altar that had been destroyed

11.question: What did Jephthah do before warring against the Ammonites?
options: He sent messengers trying to settle it in peace
He gathered all the elders of Gilead together to pray
He first consulted the priests before declaring war
He sought military support from the Philistines

11.question: According to Jephthah, whose land had Israel taken when it left Egypt?
options: The Amorites'
Moab's
Edom's
The Philistines'

11.question: What argument of time did Jephthah use against the Ammonites?
options: That Israel had dwelt in the land three hundred years
That the Ammonites had long since abandoned that land forever
That God had specifically promised that land only to Israel
That the Ammonites never had any right to the land

11.question: What vow did Jephthah make to the Lord before the battle?
options: To offer whatever first came out of his house to meet him
To build a great altar in thanksgiving for the victory achieved
To fast forty days and forty nights before entering battle
To free all of his captives as soon as he won the battle

11.question: Who came out first to meet Jephthah, tragically fulfilling the vow?
options: His only daughter
One of his loyal soldiers
His wife and his children
His hunting dog

12.title: The password 'Shibboleth'
12.text: The Ephraimites could not make the 'sh' sound and said 'Sibboleth' instead of 'Shibboleth' — which exposed them at the fords of the Jordan.

12.question: What word did the Gileadites use to identify the fleeing Ephraimites?
options: 'Shibboleth'
'Amen'
'Israel'
'Gilead'

12.question: Who judged Israel after Jephthah?
options: Ibzan
Samson
Eli
Othniel

12.question: Elon and Abdon, named at the chapter's end, were what?
options: Minor judges of Israel
Priests of the temple of Dagon
Generals of the Israelite army
Elders of the tribe of Ephraim

13.title: The Nazarite vow
13.text: Samson was to be a Nazarite from the womb: no wine, no touching anything unclean, and no cutting his hair — an outward sign of his consecration to God.

13.question: Who oppressed Israel for forty years when the angel announced Samson?
options: The Philistines
The Midianites
The Ammonites
The Moabites

13.question: What rule would govern the boy's life, according to the angel?
options: He would be a Nazarite: no wine and no razor on his hair
He would be a priest in the temple, offering sacrifices daily
He would be king of Israel and reign in great splendor
He would live in the desert, far from all his people

13.question: What did Manoah ask of the Lord after the announcement?
options: That the angel return to teach them to raise the boy
That He grant riches and prosperity to the whole family
That he show them a sign of fire coming down from the altar
That the son be born already as king of Israel

13.question: What did the angel answer when Manoah asked his name?
options: That his name was wonderful (secret)
That his name was Michael, the angel of hosts
That he would reveal it only after the offering
That his name was the same as the Lord's own name

13.question: What name was given to the boy who would begin to deliver Israel?
options: Samson
Jephthah
Gideon
Samuel

14.title: The lion and the honey
14.text: Samson killed a lion with his bare hands; later he found a swarm of bees and honey in its carcass — which inspired his wedding riddle.

14.question: What did Samson ask of his parents when he went down to Timnath?
options: A Philistine wife
An army
A field of wheat
A horse

14.question: What did Samson find in the carcass of the lion he had killed?
options: A swarm of bees and honey
A nest of venomous serpents
A hidden treasure of silver and gold
The bones of other animals

14.question: What riddle did Samson pose at the feast?
options: 'Out of the eater came forth meat, and out of the strong came sweetness'
'Out of weakness came forth strength, and out of strength came forth peace'
'Out of the rock came forth fire, and out of the fire came forth thick smoke'
'Out of the night came forth light, and out of the light came hope'

14.question: How did the Philistines learn the answer to the riddle?
options: They pressed Samson's wife to draw it out of him
They bribed a servant of Samson's house to find it out
They consulted the Philistine priests about the riddle
They guessed the answer entirely on their own

15.title: Thirst after victory
15.text: After killing a thousand Philistines, Samson nearly died of thirst; God opened a spring of water, and the place was called En-hakkore, 'the spring of him that cried.'

15.question: How did Samson destroy the Philistines' crops?
options: He loosed foxes with torches tied to their tails
He poisoned all the water wells of the whole region
He tore down the walls of the Philistine cities at night
He set fire to the stored grain barns

15.question: What did the Philistines do to Samson's wife and her father in revenge?
options: They burned them
They took them captive
They gave them gold
They drove them from the city

15.question: What did the men of Judah do to Samson to hand him over to the Philistines?
options: They bound him with new cords
They locked him in a dark dungeon
They led him chained to Gaza
They handed him to the elders

15.question: With what did Samson kill a thousand Philistines?
options: The jawbone of an ass
A cord of fresh green withes
A sharpened axe of bronze
A rather large stone

16.title: The hair that grew back
16.text: In prison, blind, Samson's hair began to grow again — and God gave him strength one last time for his avenging death.

16.question: What did Samson do with the gates of the city of Gaza?
options: He tore them off and carried them to the top of a hill
He broke them into small pieces and threw them into the sea
He handed them over to the elders of the city of Hebron
He hid them well inside a nearby cave

16.question: What did the Philistine lords ask of Delilah?
options: To find out the secret of Samson's strength
That she hand him bound over to the Philistines at night
That she find out where he hid his riches
That she convince him to move to Gaza

16.question: How many times did Samson deceive Delilah before revealing the secret?
options: Three times
Once
Seven times
Ten times

16.question: What was the secret of Samson's strength?
options: His never-cut hair, the sign of the Nazarite vow
A secret amulet given by his mother at birth
A special blessing received from the high priest
A sword forged by the angels of heaven

16.question: Where did the Philistines gather to celebrate Samson's capture?
options: In the temple of Dagon
In the king's palace
In a square of Gaza
In the desert

16.question: How did Samson kill more Philistines in his death than in his life?
options: By pulling down the temple's pillars upon them all
By poisoning the wine served at the great feast
By starting a great fire throughout the whole city
By calling neighboring armies to attack

17.title: 'Every man did what he wanted'
17.text: The refrain 'there was no king in Israel; every man did that which was right in his own eyes' sums up the whole appendix of the book (chapters 17–21).

17.question: What did Micah do with the silver he returned to his mother?
options: He had a graven image made
He bought a fertile field for his family
He donated it all to the great shrine at Shiloh
He gave it as alms to the poor of the city

17.question: What phrase sums up this disordered period of Israel?
options: 'There was no king in Israel; every man did what was right in his own eyes'
'The Lord is our king and he reigns forever over all the people of Israel'
'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is full of his glory'
'The land had rest forty years under the judge God raised up'

17.question: Whom did Micah hire to be the priest of his private shrine?
options: A young Levite
A prophet of Baal
His own son
A foreign king

18.title: The landless tribe
18.text: Dan had not yet taken possession of its inheritance; so it sent spies looking for a land to conquer.

18.question: What was the tribe of Dan seeking in this chapter?
options: A land for an inheritance
Leadership over the other tribes
A treaty of peace with Judah
A new sanctuary for worship

18.question: What did Dan's spies find at Micah's house?
options: A Levite as priest and the idols
A bronze altar with burnt offerings
An old prophet and his faithful disciples
An army hidden in the barn

18.question: How did the spies describe the city of Laish?
options: A quiet, unsuspecting people
A warlike people fully armed for battle
A fortified city full of soldiers
A wealthy but hostile people

18.question: What did Dan's 600 men carry off from Micah's house?
options: The image, the ephod and the Levite
Only the cattle and the household items
Only the priestly linen garments and robes
Only the kitchen utensils and pots

18.question: What did Micah do when he pursued the Danites who robbed him?
options: He went home, for they were too strong
He fought them and recovered everything alone
He gathered his neighbors and attacked their camp
He cursed the Danites and went home sad

18.question: What did the Danites do with Laish?
options: They took it, burned it and called it Dan
They made it a sacred city for all Israel
They returned it to its former inhabitants in peace
They rebuilt its walls and fortified it

19.title: No king, no law
19.text: This dark account opens again with 'in those days there was no king in Israel,' showing the moral collapse when every man did as he pleased.

19.question: Where did the Levite go to bring back his concubine?
options: From Beth-lehem-judah
From the mountains of Ephraim
From the city of Jebus
From Ramah in Benjamin

19.question: What did the father-in-law do to detain the Levite in Beth-lehem?
options: He urged them to stay another day
He promised him great riches if he stayed
He asked the Levite to leave early at dawn
He threatened to stop their departure by force

19.question: Why did the Levite refuse to lodge in Jebus (Jerusalem)?
options: Because it was a city of strangers, not of Israelites
Because it was a place dominated by hostile Philistines
Because it was already growing far too dark to travel safely
Because he feared ambushes from the local residents

19.question: Who took the Levite in at the street of Gibeah when no one received him?
options: An old man
The city's king
A priest
A soldier

19.question: What happened that night in Gibeah?
options: Wicked men surrounded the house and committed a great evil
The elders of the city gathered to judge the Levite publicly
The whole city held a great feast in honor of the traveler
The residents welcomed the Levite with great hospitality

19.question: What did the Levite do to call all Israel to justice?
options: He divided the body and sent the parts to the tribes
He gathered the elders and asked the priests for counsel
He built a memorial of stones at the scene of the crime
He sent a letter mourning what had happened to the judges

20.title: Inquiring of the Lord at Beth-el
20.text: After two defeats, Israel fasted and inquired of the Lord before the ark at Beth-el, where Phinehas served — only then came the victory.

20.question: Where did all Israel gather over the crime of Gibeah?
options: At Mizpah
At Shiloh
At Beth-lehem
At Jericho

20.question: What did Israel demand of the tribe of Benjamin?
options: To hand over the wicked men of Gibeah
To expel the elders of Gibeah from the city
To hand over half of its land to Israel
To pay tribute in silver and gold

20.question: What did Benjamin do instead of handing over the guilty?
options: It gathered for war against Israel
It sent secret spies to keep watch over Gibeah
It strengthened the walls of Gibeah to resist
It hid the guilty men in the city

20.question: What happened on the first day of battle?
options: Benjamin defeated Israel
Israel won easily
There was no fight
Both sides made peace

20.question: And on the second day of battle against Benjamin?
options: Israel was defeated again
Israel won with a great victory
Benjamin surrendered without fighting
There was a truce between them

20.question: What did Israel do after two defeats in a row?
options: It fasted and inquired of the Lord at Beth-el
It sent secret spies to keep watch over Gibeah
It gathered all the people to swear vengeance
It asked neighboring tribes for help

20.question: What strategy did Israel use on the third day?
options: It set an ambush around Gibeah
It sent messengers proposing peace to Benjamin
It besieged the city and cut off supplies
It attacked from the rear at dawn

20.question: What was the agreed signal of the ambush against Gibeah?
options: A pillar of smoke rising from the city
A great flash of fire coming from the camp
The sound of trumpets echoing through the mountains
A banner raised high on the mountain

20.question: What happened to the army of Benjamin?
options: It was almost entirely destroyed
It retreated in order without any losses
It surrounded Israel and defeated them
It stood firm inside the city of Gibeah

20.question: How many Benjamites escaped to the rock of Rimmon?
options: Six hundred men
Sixty men
Six thousand men
Ten thousand men

21.title: Saving a tribe
21.text: Israel had sworn not to give its daughters to Benjamin; so the tribe wouldn't vanish, it had to find a way to provide wives for the 600 survivors.

21.question: What problem arose after the war against Benjamin?
options: The tribe nearly vanished and Israel had sworn not to give them their daughters
The Benjamites demanded that Israel give them half of all their conquered lands
The Philistines took full advantage of the war to invade many of the cities of Israel
Many Benjamites refused to return and settle again in their own home cities

21.question: What did Israel do with Jabesh-gilead, which had not joined the army?
options: It took young women from it as wives for Benjamin
It destroyed nearly the whole city and spared only the elders
It imposed heavy tribute on its remaining inhabitants
It expelled its inhabitants to other lands

21.question: What did the surviving Benjamites still lack?
options: Enough wives
Land to settle in
Support from other tribes
A new territory

21.question: What solution did they find at the yearly feast of Shiloh?
options: The Benjamites would seize girls who danced at the feast
The elders would choose wives among the families of Shiloh
Each tribe would send ten young virgins to the Benjamites
It would cast lots among the neighboring cities

21.question: How does the book of Judges end?
options: 'There was no king in Israel; every man did what was right in his own eyes'
'The Lord will reign over Israel forever and there will be no more war at all'
'Joshua was crowned king and ruled over Israel with justice and great wisdom'
'Peace reigned over the whole land of Israel for many years'
